heading: A long game reopens a third sooner, a first visit’s first click no longer waits 3 s, and the benchmark now catches count regressions
recheck_change: recheck on f3a7969: reopen + cold-load, 4 pairs
recheck_only: (Reopening a long game · (navigation → record shown|game_state handled|long tasks total|next move: received)|Cold load of the start screen · desktop · (create button enabled|click at ready))
recheck_body: The commits after the 4-pair A/B changed the move list (the last two blocks first) and comments, so the two sections behind the headline results were run again on the final commit (f3a7969), 4 more pairs: reopen “record shown” 261 → 178 ms (−28%, every pair faster, 0.67 0.93 0.78 0.54; not called only because one pair was 0.93), “game_state handled → record shown” −37% and long tasks to ready −14%, both called better. Start page usable +5.1% there (1.02 1.06 1.14 0.99, not called) and −0.2% in the A/B before it: noise.
scoreboard_intro: Against main, over 4 interleaved pairs of every primary row, the branch runs at ×1.045 main’s speed and no row is called slower in any of the run’s A/Bs. The rows this run changed: reopening a 2,000-ply game −19% (−28% on the final commit, every pair faster), and the start page’s first click on a first visit, which the primary row (a median of 5 loads) cannot see: 2.7–3.7 s on main in 13 of 15 pairs, never over 2.5 s on the branch (worst 2.03 s, median about 0.25 s). One row leans slower without being called (the first pick, named under Needs from me). Against the first recorded run the primary rows are ×0.968: the 1.2× target is not met (Needs from me).
removed:
• GameHistory.boardBefore, kept only to rebuild the last move (−12 lines in history.ts); W1′’s linkInTurn left with W1′; the readme script’s guard reverted.
  • Net lines over the run (0a73938 → head, loop state excluded): +278 (+345 −67) = app client +46 (+75 −29: the touch layout’s CSS ~30 lines, comments much of the rest), app server +13, tests and e2e +141, bench and scripts +68, docs and config +10. No dependency added or removed; one config file moved (.prettierrc to the root).
choices:
• Not met: one commit per change. Three changes have a follow-up commit from the diff review (R115: d715022, 5eb3bda, 42e78f8; B1′: 30b0367, f165177; B3: 90a1da1, 3a80da8), and the readme guard is a commit and its revert. I left them rather than force-push a pushed branch; squashing the PR would put all of it in one commit on main, which breaks the rule the other way. Your call how to land it (the PR offers a split).
  • Fixed #115’s regression (an upstream change, the project’s code) before anything else, once bisected.
  • Dropped my own W1′ commit from the unpushed branch (rebuilt history) when its A/B showed play linking programs, instead of reverting it in a new commit.
  • Guarded game ids on the server only (the store operations) rather than adding a pattern to schema.json: no protocol change, no regenerated types, the client sees the same invalid_game.
  • Moved client/.prettierrc to the repo root and added bench/*.mjs to the lint (and one sentence of CLAUDE.md), after my own formatting slip.
  • On a phone held sideways, dropped “Latest”’s name while reviewing (Needs from me: taste).
  • Logged the computer’s failures to the console rather than adding words on screen (Needs from me).
  • Ran 11 lens reviewers (skipped “what’s new” and “dependencies”: nothing changed since they ran two days ago) and 3 diff reviewers (client; bench, server and CI; invariants and docs) rather than one per lens on the diff.
  • Reverted my own guard in readme-image.mjs after testing the race it guarded against: with every GPU fence held 4 s, the unchanged script still captures the whole tower.
  • Kept the touch steps at 36–38 px in the side panel rather than dropping “Latest”’s name everywhere (Needs from me).
not_confirmed:
• #115’s landing (+85%) and heap (+6%) costs: still there, cause not found (a probe rules out the move list’s scaling).
  • Real phones and GPUs: everything is SwiftShader on a 4-core VM. The first-visit click is a GPU-cache effect; on a real GPU the links are far shorter, so the gain there is smaller, unmeasured.
  • The glide marker’s saved frames have no bench row (a unit test counts them: 1 → 0).
  • The first-visit click is not called by the A/B rule (two modes); the raw table is the evidence.
  • The touch layout on a real device (rendered in Chromium with a touch pointer only).
  • What was uncommitted during the A/Bs: only bench/loop/ files, plus client/e2e/noWebGL.spec.ts (T8, a test) during the reopen recheck; the first-run and leaning-rows A/Bs ran on e8cd940, whose app code is f3a7969’s, with only loop files and tools/landing-probe/ uncommitted. The app code measured is each named commit’s.
  • Whether the texture that stays alive after 16 plies is a leak or a one-off, and where the heap’s +34% since the first run went (both seen only against 92ce041).
next:
1. R115b: #115’s per-landing (+85%) and memory (+6%) costs on a 2,000-ply game; trace the reopen section’s landing (the move list itself is ruled out).
  2. X5: one texture more alive after 16 plies than at the first run (0 → 1, on main too) and the heap at 2,000 plies +34% since then: bisect, then fix or explain.
  3. J2 with L1/J1: joining’s first board frame is 3× the first recorded run’s (5.6 s in software): the lobby’s post-pick links, the game canvas’s first frame.
  4. W1 by another road: the first pick waits on a GPU busy linking (2.3–2.6 s in software), not on the order of links; link the selection’s programs before the entrance ends.
  5. P9: the start page’s preview links the demo’s marks mid-demo (a first-visit click still met up to 1.1 s once).
  6. V5/I1: a half-open socket after a phone wakes; endless “Reconnecting” on a server error (needs words on screen).
  7. E8: the format hook for bench/*.mjs (proposed above). C9: a test that the lobby’s camera hands over on exactly the game’s first pose.
speed_line: No row is called slower in any A/B; one leans slower and is named here: the first pick after the entrance, +13% and +7.8% in two 4-pair A/Bs (pairs 0.96 1.33 1.00 1.26 · 1.02 1.06 1.30 0.96), a 2.3–2.6 s wait on the GPU in software. The branch does not touch the warm-up or the selection, but it does change code on that page (the glide marker, history, the move list), so it is not ruled out.
lean_change: recheck on e8cd940 (app = f3a7969): cold-load + move latency + select, 4 pairs
lean_only: (Cold load of the start screen · desktop · (create button enabled|click at ready → side choice shown|first load)|Move latency · (click → mover|opponent’s move: sent → first frame with it)|Selecting a piece · (click → first frame with the piece held|first pick: click))
lean_body: The 4-pair A/B left these leaning slower, uncalled: the start page’s first click (+14%), the player’s move (+4.2%), selection (+3.8%) and the first pick (+13%); on the final commit the start page was +5.1%. Four more pairs on the final code: start page +0.9%, first click +8.2% (12 vs 13 ms, pairs 0.65 1.73 1.13 1.09), the player’s move −7.4%, the opponent’s −18%, selection −6.6%, none called; the first load’s click −70%, faster in every pair. The first pick leaned slower again (+7.8%, 1.02 1.06 1.30 0.96): named above.
a4: both happen in the click’s task; stringifying the game takes 0.03 ms at 200 plies and 0.29 ms at 2,000 (measured in Node, median of 200), so nothing a player sees moves.
ci: CI: green on e8cd940; the commits since are the report, a script revert and loop files (see the PR’s checks for the head).
